problem_domain: Migrate LynkU from FastAPI+PostgreSQL+WebSocket backend to WeChat CloudBase (serverless BaaS): cloud functions for business logic, document DB for storage, watch() for real-time messaging. Replace all mock data with live database. Deep refactor of frontend to remove REST/WebSocket client layer in favor of wx.cloud SDK.

references.name: WeChat Cloud Development (CloudBase) — Deep Research
references.relevance: Comprehensive CloudBase capabilities, pricing, architecture mapping. Source: official WeChat docs + Tencent Cloud docs.
references.architecture_pattern: Serverless BaaS — client calls cloud functions (Node.js) + direct document DB access with permission rules
references.interface_style: wx.cloud.callFunction() for writes/complex queries, wx.cloud.database() for simple reads, db.collection().watch() for real-time push
references.extension_strategy: Cloud functions as single-responsibility handlers with action-based routing. Collection permissions control read/write boundaries. Workflow for visual orchestration.
references.error_handling: Cloud functions return {data, error} envelope. Client handles network errors + cloud function business errors. watch() onError for subscription failures. CloudBase auto-retry on transient failures.

key_tradeoffs.reason: No server to manage. Native WeChat auth integration. watch() replaces WebSocket. Cost: ~50 RMB/month vs server ops.
CloudBase automatically injects user identity. No token storage, no refresh logic. Simpler. Trust boundary is the WeChat runtime.
watch() is built into the client SDK. No server-side session management. Database IS the message queue for offline delivery. Trade: 1-2s latency vs true real-time.

references.name: Frontend Design Principles — LynkU
references.relevance: 14 production-grade frontend principles for CloudBase-powered mini-program. Covers layered data access, component split, watch lifecycle, setData discipline, error states, Skyline constraints.
references.architecture_pattern: Layered: Pages → Services (data access layer) → CloudBase SDK. Presentation/Container component split. Service layer as single data boundary.
references.interface_style: TypeScript-typed service modules. pages/ call services/; services/ call wx.cloud. Components receive data via properties, emit events via triggerEvent. Chaining API for Glass-Easel components.
references.extension_strategy: New pages in pages/, new components in components/. Service modules per domain (posts.ts, comments.ts, messages.ts). Subpackage for chat module.
references.error_handling: Four-state per view: loading/empty/error/loaded. Shared <empty> and <error> components. watch() onError handler mandatory. Network status monitoring via wx.onNetworkStatusChange.

key_tradeoffs.decision: Service layer vs direct DB in pages
key_tradeoffs.alternative: Call wx.cloud.database() directly in page code
key_tradeoffs.reason: Single point of change for data access. Testable. Mock-swappable during development.
setData + service layer sufficient for BBS complexity. Auth is the only global state. Add when page count >20 AND cross-page state bugs appear.
Avoid N+1 queries. Author data changes rarely. Cloud function syncs profile changes to all posts.

references.name: WeChat Mini-Program Frontend Tech Stack
references.relevance: Tech stack decision: WeChat Native (TypeScript + Skyline + Glass-Easel) over Taro/Uni-app. Confirmed for CloudBase project.
references.architecture_pattern: WeChat Native: WXML/WXSS/TS compile directly to native render calls via Skyline. Glass-Easel component framework with Chaining API + init function.
references.interface_style: Component() chaining API: .property(), .data(), .methods(), .lifetime(), .init(), .register(). setData for reactivity. WXSS with CSS variables for theming.
references.extension_strategy: Subpackages for code splitting. Custom components in components/. WeChat plugin system. No third-party framework dependency.
references.error_handling: wx.onError for global errors. Component detached() for resource cleanup. wx.reportEvent for analytics. Lifecycle-aware timer/request management.

key_tradeoffs.reason: Zero framework overhead. Full Skyline compatibility. No cross-platform requirement. Existing scaffold already native. Bundle size matters for 2MB limit.

key_tradeoffs.decision: No component library vs Vant Weapp
key_tradeoffs.reason: WeUI covers basics. Skyline compatibility issues with Vant. Add individual components only if WeUI falls short.

conclusion: CloudBase is the correct choice for LynkU at UNNC scale (~10k users). The key architectural shifts: (1) cloud functions replace FastAPI services with action-based routing, (2) document DB replaces PostgreSQL with denormalized reads, (3) watch() replaces WebSocket for real-time messaging, (4) context.OPENID replaces JWT auth flow, (5) service layer (services/) wraps all CloudBase SDK calls. Main risk: full-text search is significantly weaker (RegExp vs TSVECTOR). Acceptable for MVP; add search index collection or external search if needed. All existing frontend design principles (14 principles doc) apply directly.
